h1: About Sandstone Stucco Co: How Calgary Stucco Jobs Get Scoped
heroSub: An advertising service for Calgary homeowners. Independent stucco contractors inspect the wall, write the scope and quote you directly. Call (403) 555-0148 for a no-obligation conversation.
storyHtml:
Sandstone Stucco Co is an advertising service for homeowners in Calgary, Airdrie, Chestermere, Cochrane and Okotoks who have a stucco problem and want to reach an independent stucco contractor. The contractor inspects the wall, writes the scope and quotes you directly, and the contract is between you and them. This site is paid by contractors, does no stucco work itself, and holds no trade licence, insurance or warranty.

What this site can give you is a clear picture of how a stucco job should be scoped, so you can judge any quote you get, from anyone. Calgary Parging says on its own site that stucco is designed to deflect water, not to be waterproof, and that the layer keeping water out is the building paper behind it. Calgary Stucco and Slate says nobody can tell you the full extent of water damage until the wall is opened up. So a sound scope looks behind the surface and names where the water is getting in; see stucco repair in Calgary for the walk-through.

Two things on a stucco job can be checked before any work starts: timing and colour matching. Imasco's guide specification says to do no traditional stucco work when air and substrate temperatures are below 4°C for 24 hours before, during and after application, and ADEX's base coat bulletin sets 5°C. Imasco's datasheet also warns that colour can vary with weather, texture and method, and advises buying the same colour batch number for the whole job. A good scope therefore says how a patch will be matched, or whether a full elevation should be refinished; the hail and woodpecker page covers what to photograph and what a written scope should contain.

The site holds itself to the same standard. Every price, date and rule is traced to a source read on a stated date, prices are attributed to the firm that publishes them on the cost page, and when two sources disagree the page says so. There are no invented customers, reviews or project stories, and the site does not handle insurance claims. To talk it through, call (403) 555-0148 or use the form.

values.title: Sources you can check
values.desc: Prices are attributed to the firm that publishes them, and legal, hail and permit statements come from Alberta, City of Calgary, IBC and federal sources. If a figure has no source, it does not appear.

values.title: Scope before price
values.desc: A quote means little until someone has looked behind the finish. Pages here explain what an inspection should cover so you can compare written scopes rather than headline numbers.

values.title: Season and materials matter
values.desc: Cement and acrylic products have manufacturer temperature and curing limits, and Calgary Parging puts the season at April through October. The cold-weather pages say what can and cannot be done in winter.

values.title: Plain about limits
values.desc: No repair is promised, no claim outcome is predicted, and parging pages do not stray into foundation or structural work. The site says where its role stops and the contractor's begins.

faq.q: Is Sandstone Stucco Co a stucco contractor?
faq.a: No. It is an advertising service paid by independent stucco contractors. The contractor who inspects your wall quotes you directly and holds the contract, and the site does no stucco work and offers no warranty. In Alberta, stucco is not a compulsory-certification trade, so it is worth asking any contractor what they hold.

faq.q: What should I check before I hire a stucco contractor?
faq.a: Alberta.ca advises insisting on a written contract, getting written estimates from more than one business, and making sure the contractor and tradespeople have Workers' Compensation Board coverage. The City of Calgary says contractors need a valid City business licence, which you can confirm by calling 311. If a contractor sells in person away from their own premises and asks for money before the work is done, the Alberta prepaid contracting licence may apply, and Service Alberta has a licence search.

faq.q: Will you deal with my insurance company after hail damage?
faq.a: No. The site does not file, negotiate or manage claims, and it cannot say what an insurer will approve. IBC says hail damage is typically covered by home insurance, so check your own policy, and the City of Calgary advises contacting your insurer before you do repair work. A contractor can write a repair scope that you may give to your insurer.
